corpusSummary: A cautious synthesis of 2026 social-science studies on large language models across health, education, policy, design, and everyday decision making, highlighting human-centered interaction, safety and equity concerns, AI-enhanced research methods, and the shifting landscape of AI literacy and governance. Findings show diverse contexts but common emphasis on limitations in embodied understanding, trust, and ethical use.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and embodiment
themes.description: Across domains, studies examine user trust, perceived humanness, empathy, adoption barriers, and the effects of AI embodiment on well-being and decision making.

themes.name: AI in health information, education, and governance
themes.description: Research analyzes AI-generated health misinformation, patient education quality, clinical reasoning influence, and equity-focused governance frameworks for digital health tools.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological innovation
themes.description: LLMs are used to generate codebooks, analyze narratives, perform policy analysis, simulate social dynamics, and assist in archival and data-driven research, with calls for validation and ethics.

themes.name: AI in education and literacy for learning transformation
themes.description: Literacy, pedagogy, and assessment are rethought around GenAI, including AI tutors, teacher readiness, student engagement, and critical thinking in AI-enhanced curricula.
